title: What people frame, vi
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Monday, four days after the death certificate. A photo of a boat. The customer says it sank in '84. Wood recognizes the dock in the background and doesn't say.

panels.composition: The counter. An OLD MAN with a photograph of a fishing boat, the SANDPIPER, at a dock. BARNABY on Wood's foot — he's allowed in the shop now.

balloons.text: Sandpiper. Went down in '84 off Heceta. Everybody got off.

panels.composition: The photo. The boat. Behind it: the dock, the shack, and in a lawn chair, small, a man in a rain hood. 1983.
props: the photo: the boat, the shack, the uncle in a chair

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, close-up of a photograph of a fishing boat at a dock with a shingle shack behind and a small figure in a rain hood sitting in a lawn chair
image.notes: The uncle in the photo, twenty years younger, in the same chair. Died four days ago in the strip's world. Wood sees it. Nobody says.

panels.composition: Wood looking at the photo longer than the job needs. The dog looking up at him.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a young man looking at a photograph a beat too long while a dog looks up at him from his foot, no words

panels.composition: The framed boat. The old man taking it. Wood's eyes on the small figure in the chair as it goes out the door.
panels.caption: Monday.
